title: An Earthenware Mug, a 1942 Bomb Crater, an Industrially Reinforced Piano, and Geoff queer Music Therapy
author: Geoffa Fells
description:
To manage the extremely painful emotions arising in response to the ableist, pathologising, classist, heteronormative and racist content in music therapy training, I wrote my essays as consecutive scenes of a play - now 4 scenes! Child development, attachment theory, relational dynamics and therapeutic approaches are all queered via an intersectionally anti-oppressive lens by neurodivergent characters. The narrative opens with a neuroqueer family in North London, heads out to the International Space Station and concludes with a Whodunnit set in IKEA.


Weeks in to my studies, it was noted by the tutors that some of the music therapy course content was actively harmful to me as a trans non-binary, autistic, disabled person from a working class background... "in order to best include you, we don't think you should come in" said my head of department. Queer people face many barriers in accessing queer-affirming therapy and these barriers are rooted in the barriers faced by queer people training in therapy. I'm hoping that my play will generate awareness and discussion around this.

title: Catholic Convos Podcast
author: pauliedamato
description:
Faith is often presented as something we’re supposed to have all the answers to. But what happens when we have questions? What happens when we doubt, struggle, disagree, or simply don’t understand?

This podcast is a place for those questions.

Our goal is to create honest, respectful, and meaningful conversations about Catholicism, Christianity, faith, doubt, and the questions that people sometimes feel uncomfortable asking out loud. We believe that asking questions doesn’t make someone a bad Catholic—or a bad Christian. In many cases, asking questions can be the beginning of a deeper understanding of what we believe and why we believe it.

Throughout the podcast, we’ll explore questions from many different perspectives. We’ll talk about the questions atheists and non-believers have about Catholicism, as well as the doubts that Catholics themselves may quietly wrestle with. We’ll discuss difficult topics, examine Church teachings, and take a closer look at the reasons behind the Catholic faith.

And most importantly, we want to have these conversations honestly.

Our hope is not to tell people what they are allowed to ask or what they are supposed to think. Instead, we want to create a space where curiosity is welcomed, doubts can be discussed, and faith can be explored without fear of judgment.

With guests such as Father Meinders, we’ll have conversations that encourage listeners to think deeply, challenge their assumptions, and perhaps even see their faith from a different perspective.

Whether you are a practicing Catholic, someone who has walked away from the Church, someone who is questioning your beliefs, an atheist who wants to understand Catholicism, or simply someone who has always had questions, you are welcome here.

Because sometimes the questions we’re most afraid to ask are the ones worth asking the most.

Listen. Question. Explore. Believe—or wrestle with what you believe.

There are no perfect questions, and there may not always be simple answers. But there is always room for an honest conversation.

title: The War in Between
author: Richard L Burr
description:
The War in Between
In 1990, Congress set up a commission to study every major fight of the Civil War — three hundred eighty-four fields in all — and rank each one by how much it actually weighed on the war. Class A. Class B. You already know most of those: Gettysburg, Antietam, Vicksburg.
The War in Between stays entirely in Class C: real fights, real ground, almost none of it known outside the county it happened in. A Union general who broke his own standing orders and missed an entire brigade hiding in the trees three days before Bull Run. A sitting governor who personally commanded troops in a battle — the only time in American history that's happened. A herd of wild horses, mistaken in the dark for enemy cavalry, on a beach in Florida.
Episodes run in strict order, one year at a time, coast to coast — Virginia one week, Missouri or Kansas the next — because the war didn't happen in one place at a time, and neither does this show. If you already know the big campaigns, this is the thread that ties them together: the days you skipped on your way to the days everyone else knows by heart.
Every episode ends the same way.
Know this ground.

What lights you up—and what have you stopped making space for?

When life knocked the stuffing out of me, survival mode showed up as me disappearing. My world got very small, and so did I. But my story isn't over. I am done just existing.

The Nerve of You is me coming out of hiding and having the nerve to find my voice at 56. It’s a playful experiment. It could be messy, it could be raw, it could be exactly the tonic you need, and it’s very likely to be random as the real me returns and the jitters wear off. As long as I’m enjoying the process and feeling alive, that’s hitting the jackpot.

Perfectionism isn't invited, but you are. Join me in making space for what lights you up and makes you feel fully alive.

On this show, we’re exploring:

  • Curiosity over Perfection: Learning to play, experiment, and come out of hiding

  • Identity: Owning the truth that there’s nothing wrong with you (except your thinking that there is)

  • Nervous System Supports: Creative ways to build new responses and cultivate an inner ease as you become visible

  • The Magic of Fascia Release: Melting holding patterns in the body to create physical, mental, and emotional space

  • Plant-Fueled Living: Delicious plant-based meals, treats made with natural sugars and DIY skincare your body loves

So, if you’re ready to set your Supporting Role Oscar down and make space for you and all your fabulous idiosyncrasies, you’re in the right place.

Grab a cuppa and hit subscribe, let’s see where this takes us.

Knowing how to ask better questions, evaluate information, make decisions, communicate effectively, think strategically, and work with AI systems may become just as important as traditional technical expertise.We explore how individuals and organizations can adapt to this new environment.You'll discover practical strategies for learning AI, developing valuable skills, improving productivity, building AI-powered workflows, understanding emerging technologies, and preparing for the changing job market.We also examine the rise of AI agents and autonomous systems and what they mean for education and professional development.As AI begins performing increasingly complex tasks, the definition of expertise itself is changing. The advantage may shift from simply knowing information to knowing how to apply judgment, context, creativity, strategy, and human insight alongside intelligent machines.Whether you're learning AI for the first time, developing your career, building a business, teaching others, or preparing for the future of work, The AI Learning Advantage provides practical insights designed to help you stay ahead of technological change.This is not simply a podcast about artificial intelligence.It is a podcast about how humans can become more capable in an AI-powered world.

title: The Obvious Myth
author: SARA
description:
This is the Obvious Myth - for anyone who's ever felt like their business should be performing better than it is, and suspected the answer wasn't more leads.

They almost never are. The Obvious Myth is a solo video podcast for founders and operators who've solved for demand and are still wondering why the business isn't performing the way it should. Each episode takes one specific, relatable story — a viral order spike, a CRM nobody trusts, a founder who wouldn't accept a plane until he understood why it failed its own tests — and uses it to expose the mid-funnel system problem hiding underneath. Season 1 follows Claire and Jamie's business from its first messy map to a fully rebuilt system, alongside a handful of founders and operators with problems that follow the same patterns. By the finale, ten myths resolve into one repeatable method — Clarify, Organize, Route, Expand — for building a business that can grow without its founder being the ceiling.

Grounded, honest, and deeply rooted in our local soil, Alamance County Life offers a thoughtful, unfiltered look at the milestones, conflicts, and human stories that forged our home. Subscribe today and join us as we uncover the true history lying just beneath our feet.
